# @cstack-dev/convex-s3

> A Convex component for S3-compatible storage (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO). Browsers upload straight to the bucket with presigned tickets; Convex signs requests inside the component, enforces the app's checks and records what arrived. API modeled on the Convex R2 component. Import it as `@cstack-dev/convex-s3`, never `convex-s3`.

This file is an integration guide for coding agents. Follow the steps in order. Human-oriented docs: https://github.com/christianstamati/convex-s3/tree/main/packages/convex-s3#readme

## Entry points

- `@cstack-dev/convex-s3`: `S3` class (server), types (`UploadTicket`, `ObjectMetadata`, `PutOptions`, `UploadPolicy`, `UploadRequest`, `GetUrlOptions`, `ClientApiOptions`), validators (`vObjectMetadata`, `vUploadTicket`), helpers (`newKey`, `normalizePrefix`, `cleanFileName`).
- `@cstack-dev/convex-s3/convex.config`: the component, for `app.use()` in `convex/convex.config.ts`.
- `@cstack-dev/convex-s3/react`: `useUploadFile(api.<module>)`, and `uploadFile(client, api, file, options)` outside React.
- `@cstack-dev/convex-s3/testing`: `FakeS3` (in-memory S3) and `register(t)` for convex-test.

## Step 0: check the project

1. `convex` in package.json must be >= 1.46.0 (components with their own env vars). Upgrade if older.
2. Find the app's auth (Convex Auth `getAuthUserId`, Clerk `ctx.auth.getUserIdentity()`, ...). The checks in step 4 must use it. If the app has no auth, say so to the user and rate-limit uploads (see Rules).
3. Find the Convex deployment's region if possible (Dashboard > Settings, or the URL, e.g. `*.eu-west-1.convex.cloud`) and use the same AWS region for the bucket.
4. Ask the user which provider they want if unclear. Default: AWS S3 with the AWS CLI. Check `aws sts get-caller-identity` works; if not, ask the user to sign in (`aws login` or `aws configure sso`). Never ask for or handle their AWS password.

## Step 1: create the bucket and its IAM user (AWS CLI)

Pick a globally unique bucket name, e.g. `<app>-files-<account id>`. Use the user's dev origin (usually `http://localhost:3000` or `http://localhost:5173`) and their production origin in CORS.

```sh
BUCKET=<app>-files-<account id>
REGION=<region>
aws s3api create-bucket --bucket $BUCKET --region $REGION --create-bucket-configuration LocationConstraint=$REGION
# In us-east-1, omit --create-bucket-configuration.
aws s3api put-public-access-block --bucket $BUCKET --public-access-block-configuration BlockPublicAcls=true,IgnorePublicAcls=true,BlockPublicPolicy=true,RestrictPublicBuckets=true
aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket $BUCKET --cors-configuration '{"CORSRules":[{"AllowedOrigins":["http://localhost:3000"],"AllowedMethods":["PUT","POST","GET","HEAD"],"AllowedHeaders":["*"],"ExposeHeaders":["ETag"],"MaxAgeSeconds":3600}]}'
aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket $BUCKET --lifecycle-configuration '{"Rules":[{"ID":"abort-incomplete-multipart","Status":"Enabled","Filter":{"Prefix":""},"AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload":{"DaysAfterInitiation":1}}]}'
aws iam create-user --user-name $BUCKET-convex
aws iam put-user-policy --user-name $BUCKET-convex --policy-name bucket --policy-document '{"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:PutObject","s3:GetObject","s3:DeleteObject","s3:AbortMultipartUpload","s3:ListMultipartUploadParts","s3:PutObjectTagging","s3:GetObjectTagging"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::'$BUCKET'/*"},{"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:ListBucket","s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads"],"Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::'$BUCKET'"}]}'
```

- CORS must allow headers `*` and expose `ETag` (multipart uploads read part ETags in the browser).
- Keep Block Public Access on. For public files, put CloudFront in front (origin access control) and set `S3_PUBLIC_URL` later.
- Create the access key in step 3, piping it straight into Convex. Never print the secret.

Other providers: Cloudflare R2 (`S3_REGION=auto`, `S3_ENDPOINT=https://<account id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`; no POST uploads, no object tags; CORS in the R2 dashboard; the user creates an R2 API token with Object Read & Write on the bucket). MinIO (`S3_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000`, path-style by default). Any provider must support conditional writes (`If-None-Match: *`).

## Step 2: install and register the component

```sh
npm install @cstack-dev/convex-s3
```

`convex/convex.config.ts` (merge into the existing file; keep other components):

```ts
import { defineApp } from "convex/server"
import { v } from "convex/values"
import s3 from "@cstack-dev/convex-s3/convex.config"

const app = defineApp({
  env: {
    S3_BUCKET: v.string(),
    S3_REGION: v.string(),
    S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: v.string(),
    S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: v.string(),
    S3_ENDPOINT: v.optional(v.string()),
    S3_PUBLIC_URL: v.optional(v.string()),
  },
})

app.use(s3, {
  env: {
    S3_BUCKET: app.env.S3_BUCKET,
    S3_REGION: app.env.S3_REGION,
    S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID: app.env.S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID,
    S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: app.env.S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY,
    S3_ENDPOINT: app.env.S3_ENDPOINT,
    S3_PUBLIC_URL: app.env.S3_PUBLIC_URL,
  },
})

export default app
```

If the app already calls `defineApp({ env: { ... } })`, add these keys to it. Optional extras the component also accepts: `S3_SESSION_TOKEN`, `S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE`.

## Step 3: set the env vars on the deployment

Required env vars must exist before `convex dev` can push. Set them without printing secrets: pipe them over stdin in .env format.

```sh
read -r KEY_ID SECRET < <(aws iam create-access-key --user-name $BUCKET-convex --query 'AccessKey.[AccessKeyId,SecretAccessKey]' --output text | tr -d '\r')
printf "S3_BUCKET='%s'\nS3_REGION='%s'\nS3_ACCESS_KEY_ID='%s'\nS3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY='%s'\n" "$BUCKET" "$REGION" "$KEY_ID" "$SECRET" | npx convex env set --force
unset KEY_ID SECRET
```

- On Windows, CLIs print CRLF: the `tr -d '\r'` matters (the component trims values too, but strip anyway).
- Run it in the directory with the Convex project (where `convex/` and `.env.local` are). Production: add `--prod`, or set them in the dashboard.
- If the user prefers, they can run `npx convex env set S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` themselves (it prompts).

## Step 4: the storage module

Create `convex/files.ts` (name it after what the app stores; `callbacks` must be this module's path). Adapt the checks to the app's auth and rules:

```ts
import { S3 } from "@cstack-dev/convex-s3"
import { ConvexError, v } from "convex/values"
import { components } from "./_generated/api"
import type { DataModel } from "./_generated/dataModel"
import { mutation, query } from "./_generated/server"
import { getAuthUserId } from "@convex-dev/auth/server" // use the app's auth

export const s3 = new S3(components.s3)

const MAX_SIZE = 100 * 1024 * 1024

export const {
  generateUploadUrl,
  syncMetadata,
  createMultipartUpload,
  signUploadParts,
  listUploadedParts,
  completeMultipartUpload,
  abortUpload,
  onSyncMetadata,
} = s3.clientApi<DataModel>({
  checkUpload: async (ctx, _bucket, request) => {
    const userId = await getAuthUserId(ctx)
    if (userId === null) throw new ConvexError("Sign in to upload")
    if (request.size > MAX_SIZE) throw new ConvexError("Files can be 100 MB at most")
    return { prefix: `users/${userId}/`, maxSize: MAX_SIZE }
  },
  onUpload: async (ctx, _bucket, key, metadata) => {
    const userId = await getAuthUserId(ctx)
    if (userId === null) throw new ConvexError("Sign in to upload")
    await ctx.db.insert("files", {
      owner: userId,
      key,
      name: key.split("/").pop() ?? key,
      size: metadata.size,
      contentType: metadata.contentType,
    })
  },
  callbacks: "files",
})

export const list = query({
  args: {},
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    const userId = await getAuthUserId(ctx)
    if (userId === null) return []
    return await ctx.db
      .query("files")
      .withIndex("by_owner", (q) => q.eq("owner", userId))
      .order("desc")
      .take(100)
  },
})

export const downloadUrl = mutation({
  args: { id: v.id("files") },
  handler: async (ctx, { id }) => {
    const userId = await getAuthUserId(ctx)
    const file = await ctx.db.get(id)
    if (file === null || file.owner !== userId) throw new ConvexError("File not found")
    return await s3.getUrl(ctx, file.key, {
      expiresIn: 5 * 60,
      responseContentDisposition: `attachment; filename="${file.name.replace(/["\\]/g, "_")}"`,
    })
  },
})

export const remove = mutation({
  args: { id: v.id("files") },
  handler: async (ctx, { id }) => {
    const userId = await getAuthUserId(ctx)
    const file = await ctx.db.get(id)
    if (file === null || file.owner !== userId) throw new ConvexError("File not found")
    await ctx.db.delete(id)
    await s3.deleteObject(ctx, file.key)
  },
})
```

Add the app table to `convex/schema.ts`:

```ts
files: defineTable({
  owner: v.id("users"),
  key: v.string(),
  name: v.string(),
  size: v.number(),
  contentType: v.optional(v.string()),
}).index("by_owner", ["owner"]),
```

Notes:
- Export every function `clientApi()` returns that the UI needs. `useUploadFile` needs `generateUploadUrl` and `syncMetadata`, plus the five multipart functions for files above 64 MB. `onSyncMetadata` must be exported when `onUpload` or `onSyncMetadata` is used.
- `clientApi()` can also return `getMetadata`, `listMetadata` and `deleteObject`; each needs its check (`checkReadKey`, `checkReadBucket`, `checkDelete`) or it refuses to run. Most apps use their own table instead, as above.
- `checkUpload` may return `{ prefix, key, maxSize, contentType, put, multipartThreshold, partSize }`. The browser's `request.prefix` counts only if returned as `prefix`.

## Step 5: the upload UI (React)

```tsx
import { useUploadFile } from "@cstack-dev/convex-s3/react"
import { useMutation, useQuery } from "convex/react"
import { useState } from "react"
import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api"

export function Files() {
  const uploadFile = useUploadFile(api.files)
  const files = useQuery(api.files.list) ?? []
  const downloadUrl = useMutation(api.files.downloadUrl)
  const remove = useMutation(api.files.remove)
  const [progress, setProgress] = useState<number | null>(null)

  return (
    <div>
      <input
        type="file"
        onChange={async (event) => {
          const file = event.target.files?.[0]
          if (!file) return
          setProgress(0)
          try {
            await uploadFile(file, { onProgress: ({ fraction }) => setProgress(fraction) })
          } finally {
            setProgress(null)
            event.target.value = ""
          }
        }}
      />
      {progress !== null && <progress value={progress} />}
      <ul>
        {files.map((file) => (
          <li key={file._id}>
            {file.name}
            <button onClick={async () => window.location.assign(await downloadUrl({ id: file._id }))}>Download</button>
            <button onClick={() => remove({ id: file._id })}>Delete</button>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
    </div>
  )
}
```

`uploadFile(file, { onProgress, signal, concurrency, resume })` returns the key. Pass an `AbortController`'s `signal` to cancel. The app must be inside `ConvexProvider` (or `ConvexAuthProvider`).

## Step 6: verify

1. `npx convex dev --once` pushes without errors (an error about missing env vars means step 3 didn't run on this deployment).
2. Run the app, upload a small file and one over 64 MB if possible, download it, delete it.
3. Optional tests: see Testing below.

## Rules and pitfalls

- Import from `@cstack-dev/convex-s3` (and its `/react`, `/convex.config`, `/testing` entry points). There is no package named `convex-s3`.
- Never put AWS credentials in code, function arguments, logs or chat. They live only in the deployment's env vars.
- Don't sign URLs in list queries: a subscribed query keeps its result, so URLs expire on screen. Sign them in a mutation when clicked (`downloadUrl` above), or use public URLs (`S3_PUBLIC_URL`, `s3.getPublicUrl(ctx, key)`).
- Serve untrusted uploads as attachments (`responseContentDisposition: "attachment; ..."`). Never open user-uploaded HTML or SVG inline.
- `callbacks` is a string: the module's path (`"files"`, `"storage/files"`), not `internal.files` (a circular type).
- `generateUploadUrl` requires `size`; `useUploadFile` sends it.
- Tickets refuse to overwrite (`If-None-Match: *`). To replace an object at a fixed key, return `put: { ifNoneMatch: false }` from `checkUpload`. Use `s3.isKeyInUse(ctx, key)` before picking a key yourself.
- Methods take `ctx` first: `s3.getUrl(ctx, key)`, `s3.store(ctx, blob, options)`, `s3.deleteObject(ctx, key)`.
- Network S3 calls (`store`, `syncMetadata`, `headObject`, `getObject`, `listObjects`, `copyObject`, `moveObject`) run in actions. `getUrl`, `getMetadata`, `listMetadata`, `listFolder`, `isKeyInUse` work anywhere; `deleteObject`, `deleteObjects`, `deletePrefix` and `generateUploadUrl` need a mutation or action.
- Without auth, anyone can upload. Rate-limit `checkUpload` (e.g. `@convex-dev/rate-limiter`) and keep `maxSize` small.
- Prefixes are raw: `users/1` matches `users/12/`. End folder prefixes with `/`.

## Server API (S3 class)

- `generateUploadUrl(ctx, { key | prefix + fileName, size, maxSize, contentType, ...putOptions, multipartThreshold, partSize, expiresIn })` -> ticket
- `generateUploadPost(ctx, { key | prefix + fileName, maxSize, minSize, contentType })` -> POST ticket (not on R2)
- `store(ctx, blob | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array, { key | prefix + fileName, contentType, ... })` -> key (action; multipart above 64 MB)
- `syncMetadata(ctx, key)` -> `{ metadata, isNew }` (action)
- `getUrl(ctx, key, { expiresIn, versionId, responseContentDisposition, responseContentType, responseCacheControl })` -> URL
- `getPublicUrl(ctx, key)` -> URL or null; `isKeyInUse(ctx, key)` -> boolean
- `getMetadata(ctx, key)`, `listMetadata(ctx, limit, cursor, prefix)`, `pageMetadata(ctx, paginationOpts, prefix)`
- `listFolder(ctx, prefix, { delimiter, limit, cursor })` -> `{ folders, objects, isTruncated, cursor }` (live, one level)
- `deleteObject(ctx, key)`, `deleteObjects(ctx, keys)`, `deletePrefix(ctx, prefix)`
- Actions: `headObject(ctx, key)`, `getObject(ctx, key, { range })`, `listObjects(ctx, { prefix, delimiter, cursor, limit })`, `copyObject(ctx, from, to, put?)`, `moveObject(ctx, from, to, put?)`, `putObjectTagging(ctx, key, tags)`

Put options: `contentType`, `cacheControl`, `contentDisposition`, `contentEncoding`, `contentLanguage`, `metadata` (printable ASCII; `upload-ticket` is reserved), `tagging`, `storageClass`, `serverSideEncryption`, `kmsKeyId`, `checksumSha256` (single uploads only), `ifNoneMatch` (default true).

## Testing

```ts
// convex/test.setup.ts
import { FakeS3, register } from "@cstack-dev/convex-s3/testing"
import { convexTest } from "convex-test"
import { vi } from "vitest"
import schema from "./schema"

export const modules = import.meta.glob("./**/*.ts")

export function setup() {
  const s3 = new FakeS3()
  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(s3.env())) vi.stubEnv(name, value)
  vi.stubGlobal("fetch", s3.fetch)
  const t = convexTest(schema, modules)
  register(t)
  return { t, s3 }
}
```

`vitest.config.ts` needs `test: { environment: "edge-runtime", server: { deps: { inline: ["convex-test", "@cstack-dev/convex-s3"] } } }`. In a test, a browser upload is: `const ticket = await t.mutation(api.files.generateUploadUrl, { fileName, size, contentType })`, then `await fetch(ticket.url, { method: "PUT", headers: ticket.headers, body })`, then `await t.action(api.files.syncMetadata, { key: ticket.key, token: ticket.token })`.
